newsitem.title: INDIA: Seven political workers gunned down in Kashmir.
newsitem.headline: Seven political workers gunned down in Kashmir.

text.p: Unidentified militants shot dead seven activists of Kashmir's largest pro-India political party days before it takes office as the first elected government in nearly a decade, police said on Sunday.
Police in India's troubled northern state of Jammu and Kashmir said the militants on Saturday gunned down five men and two women supporters of the National Conference party.
The party last week won 57 places in the state's 87-member assembly in the first elections since a separatist revolt broke out in 1990.

The unidentified gunmen arrived in a taxi, the police said. They forced their way into two homes in Saderkoot village, near Sumbal, 35 km (21.75 miles) north of Srinagar. They fired indiscriminately on the occupants, the police added.
"It is a serious matter, we strongly condemn it," the party spokesman Saifuddin Soz told Reuters.
"We are discussing it at a very high level," he added, but gave no details of the action his party would take.

The area is a stronghold of pro-India militant groups, officials said. It lies in the constituency of Kukka Parrey, the leader of the Jammu Kashmir Ikhwan group, who won the polls as a candidate of the Awami League, the group's political arm.

Over a dozen militant groups in the state are fighting for self-determination or closer ties to neighbouring Pakistan. At least three pro-India militant groups are helping Indian paramilitary troops combat militancy.

National Conference chief Farooq Abdullah, who will be sworn in as the state's chief minister on Tuesday, has said he will deal with separatist militants with a firm hand, though he is ready to enter into talks with unarmed separatists.

Abdullah was one of more than a dozen candidates who escaped attacks on their lives during the month-long campaign that preceded the polls. At least 21 political activists died in the accompanying violence, police estimate.
Eleven separatist guerrillas and two civilians were killed in two different gun battles with Indian para-military troops during the last 24 hours, police said.
Suspected separatist militants also shot dead one person in the downtown Srinagar area of Butakadal on Saturday, local newspapers said.
More than 20,000 people have died in insurgency-related violence since 1990, when the separatist revolt flared, official sources say.
